Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A quick recap from our side and a couple of follow-ups so we can size this properly:

- Target latency: p95 <= 200–250 ms for single-turn generation (average response ~35–50 tokens).
- Throughput / concurrency: steady-state ~150 concurrent requests, with predictable spikes up to ~300 concurrent requests during clinic hours.
- Streaming: we need token-level streaming for partial results in the UI (UX requirement). Latency of first-byte is particularly important.
- Payload: short prompts + patient metadata (~1–2 KB).

Two asks: can you share recommended levers to meet the latency SLO while keeping cost within our budget, and a rough ballpark for cost at our expected scale (monthly 10M tokens / peak concurrency above)?

I'll attach a short sample prompt set in a follow-up — Priya will own the technical deep-dive scheduling.

Thanks,

Tom — thanks for the clear recap. Recap + next steps below. I attached a short one-pager (orchid-slo-cost-levers.pdf) that summarizes the levers we discussed.

Quick recap:
- SLO: p95 <= 200–250ms, streaming-first-byte is mission-critical, avg output ~40 tokens.
- Load profile: steady 150 concurrent, burst to 300.

Initial recommendations (high level):
1) Model variant selection: start with a 13B model (cost-efficient) with an option to fall back to a quantized 70B variant for critical requests that need higher quality. We typically recommend: Llama-2-13B (8-bit) for baseline, Llama-2-70B (4-bit quant) as a quality-tier.
2) Continuous batching: enable an aggressive continuous-batching window (~5–10ms) to maximize GPU utilization while keeping first-byte latency low.
3) Prefix / KV caching: cache common prompt prefixes (patient intake templates, standard system prompts) to avoid repeated compute and reduce token work.
4) Quantization profiles: 8-bit for baseline, 4-bit for heavy-duty quality mode; test for quality regressions via evals.
5) Dedicated capacity + autoscaling buffer: reserve a baseline dedicated pool to meet steady-state concurrency, with burst autoscaling for spikes; warm workers to keep KV cache hot for lowest latencies.
6) Streaming optimizations: prioritize sending first tokens immediately (small initial micro-batch) and use a short batching window for subsequent tokens.

Rough cost ballpark (very high-level):
- Baseline (13B, quant 8-bit) running steady 150 conc: ~ $X per 100k requests (we'll run exact sims once we have sample payloads).
- Mixed strategy with 10% falling back to 70B (4-bit): ~ +20–30% cost.

Next steps / asks:
- Rishi to run a quick microbenchmark/estimate (see cc).
- Please send sample payloads and representative traffic distribution (token length, % streaming vs single-turn).
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive next week to align on perf tests (Rishi + infra). Priya — are you available Wed 7/7 or Thu 7/8?

Attaching: orchid-slo-cost-levers.pdf (summary + example configs). Also linking a short HubSpot record so we can track follow-ups.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Adding a few concrete engineering notes and config suggestions to help with sizing / tests:

- Batching & latency: target a continuous-batching window of ~6–8ms. For first-byte streaming, use an initial micro-batch that emits as soon as the first logits are ready, then accumulate small batches for throughput. This typically preserves p95 while keeping cost efficient.
- KV / prefix caching: warm the KV cache for top-20 common prefixes (clinic templates, system prompts). Cache hits can reduce per-request compute by ~25–40% depending on prompt overlap.
- Quantization tradeoffs: 8-bit quant is usually a safe baseline for 13B; 4-bit for 70B yields big cost savings but requires careful evals for hallucination/quality. We can run A/B evals against your sample prompts.
- Dedicated pool sizing (ballpark): for 13B optimized runtime, ~3 x A100-80GB equiv nodes should cover steady 150 conc with our continuous-batching config; add 1–2 nodes for warm capacity to handle 300-concurrency spikes with autoscale. If you opt for L40S-class GPUs or newer L-series, we can reduce node count. Exact counts will vary with sequence lengths and streaming patterns.
- Observability: we'll instrument per-route p95/p99, first-byte latency, and batch sizes. Also recommend tracing for early-byte emit times so we can tune micro-batch thresholds.

What I need from you to produce an accurate estimate:
1) Representative sample set (Prompts + expected response length distribution).
2) Expected % of requests that must be streaming-first-byte vs non-streaming.
3) Typical tokenization characteristics (avg input tokens).

I'll queue a short microbenchmark run once we have a sample bundle — should take 24–48 hours to get preliminary numbers back.

—Rishi
